subject: Post-call: ops handshake, commitment checklist and fallback plan
messages:
From: jasmine_liu
To: Kris Patel <kris@heliomed.com>
Cc: ben_carter, rishi_malhotra, naomi_feldman
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ops handshake, commitment checklist and fallback plan

Kris — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency at peak and strict PHI isolation requirements for inference.
- Goal: production inference with 200 req/s sustained, 500 req/s burst, <120ms tail latency for p50/p95, SLA target 99.9% availability for inference endpoints.
- Ask: procurement target ~6 weeks; want a clear ops handshake (MOP) and fallback story for capacity constraints.

Key points from the call
- Workload and constraints: models will be quantized LLMs (7–13B family). You need tenant-level isolation (PHI) and VPC peering into your environment. Data retention: 30 days for logs, model inputs must not be cached beyond session.
- Throughput & latency: Production plan is 200 sustained QPS with 500 burstable. You're sensitive to p95 latency spikes during peak inference windows (batching must not add >40ms median overhead).
- Reliability: Targeting 99.9% inference availability and a defined RTO/RPO for incidents. Secondary model fallback acceptable for degraded quality but must maintain latency.
- Security/compliance: Must integrate with customer KMS, provide audit logs for inference requests, and deliver SOC2 artifacts during procurement.

What Redwood proposes (initial outline)
1) Dedicated reserved pool (isolated tenant pool) sized for target throughput — we'll propose node counts & GPU types after reviewing recent traffic samples.
2) Canary rollout + staged canary traffic (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with an ops MOP that includes rollback and auto-fallback to a compatible quantized variant.
3) SLA draft: 99.9% availability for the endpoint, with latency SLOs measured at p95 and an agreed credit formula for misses.
4) Burst policy: burst to shared capacity for short windows (with throttles), plus pre-warmed warm-pool to reduce cold-starts.

Immediate next steps / asks (owner in parentheses)
- Share 7 days of production traffic (sample) — Kris / HelioMed (Kris) — due EOD Thu 7/2
- Redwood to send: draft MOP + SLO spreadsheet + preliminary sizing and pricing (Jasmine) — by Tue 7/6
- Schedule technical deep-dive on network/KMS integration (Ben + Rishi + HelioMed infra) — propose Wed 7/7 10:00 PT
- Procurement: Alyssa to share PO template and procurement constraints (Alyssa) — by 7/9

Attachments: MOP-draft.pdf (ops checklist), SLO-targets-helio.xlsx (SLA and latency buckets), pricing-term-sheet-v1.pdf (initial commercial terms).

If that matches your read, we'll kick off the technical deep-dive and circulate a mutual action plan. If any of the numbers above are off, tell me now and we'll adjust.

Thanks — Jasmine

--

From: Kris Patel <kris@heliomed.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops handshake, commitment checklist and fallback plan

Thanks Jasmine — useful summary. A couple clarifications from my side:

1) Fallback behavior: can you outline exactly what "compatible quantized variant" means operationally? We need to know quality degradation bounds (ROUGE/EM/throughput tradeoff) and how rollback will be triggered.
2) KMS: we require customer-managed keys with key rotation. Any workarounds if our HSM vendor requires additional networking?
3) Canary: want a concrete canary duration (we usually run 48–72h at each step) and a health matrix for automated failover.

Procurement: Alyssa will share our PO template later this week. We're targeting internal sign-off in 5–6 weeks, but that's dependent on the ops/runbook and SOC2 evidence.

If you can send the draft MOP and the SLO sheet ASAP it will help our security/compliance review. Let's tentatively lock Wed 7/7 10:00 PT for the network deep-dive; Ben — are you free?

Best,
Kris
CTO, HelioMed
